title: WHY THIS HEDGEHOG COVERS ITS SPINES IN FOAM
caption: Hedgehogs sometimes spread frothy saliva on their spines. Scientists are still studying why. 🦔 #Hedgehog #AnimalFacts #Wildlife #NatureFacts #WildVox

narration_timeline.text: That walking pincushion is not looking for a fight.
narration_timeline.scene: Open on a real European hedgehog moving naturally

narration_timeline.text: The European hedgehog uses thousands of stiff spines as armor, but it spends most nights hunting invertebrates with its nose close to the ground.
narration_timeline.scene: Show nighttime foraging while the narration discusses spines and hunting

narration_timeline.text: When frightened, it curls into a tight ball, hiding its soft belly.
narration_timeline.scene: Switch to the curled-ball behavior at the exact spoken cue

narration_timeline.text: Sometimes it self-anoints: after tasting a new smell, it spreads frothy saliva over its spines.
narration_timeline.scene: Show authentic self-anointing during the self-anointing explanation
Use a calm authentic hedgehog shot while uncertainty is explained

narration_timeline.text: The punchline? A tiny garden visitor has one of nature's strangest grooming routines.
narration_timeline.scene: Finish with a strong hedgehog payoff shot
